deploy.content: is wholemeal bread the same as wholemeal flour

No. Wholemeal flour is the ground grain with the bran and germ still in it, and that is the whole of what it is. Wholemeal bread is what you get after that flour is mixed with yeast, water, salt and usually a bit of fat or sugar, then proved and baked. So one is an ingredient and the other is a finished thing made from it, which matters if a recipe calls for one and you have the other.

Plain flour is milled from the same wheat but with the bran and germ taken out, so it is finer, lighter and paler, and it keeps far longer because the oily germ is what goes rancid. It is lower in protein than bread flour, which is the important bit in practice, since protein is what forms the structure that traps gas. That is why plain flour is the right choice for cakes, pancakes and pastry, where you want tenderness rather than chew, and the wrong choice for a loaf, which will come out dense and squat because there is not enough structure to hold the rise. It is called all purpose in some countries, which is the same thing under a different name.
